feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=-4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-3y.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[0.2,\,0.3]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-3y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(-4{x}^{2}y+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-3y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8xy+2x+2 \\ -4{x}^{2}+2y-3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(-8xy+2x+2) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(-4{x}^{2}+2y-3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(-8xy+2x+2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(-4{x}^{2}+2y-3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8y+2 & -8x \\ -8x & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}-8y+2 & -8x \\ -8x & 2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-8xy+2x+2 \\ -4{x}^{2}+2y-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}-8y+2 & -8x \\ -8x & 2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-8xy+2x+2 \\ -4{x}^{2}+2y-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 0.3\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-8(0.3)+2 & -8(0.2) \\ -8(0.2) & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-8(0.2)(0.3)+2(0.2)+2 \\ -4(0.2)^{2}+2(0.3)-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 0.3\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-0.4 & -1.6 \\ -1.6 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1.92 \\ -2.56\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 0.3\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-0.4)\cdot 2-(-1.6)\cdot (-1.6)}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1.6 \\ 1.6 & -0.4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1.92 \\ -2.56\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 0.3\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{3.36}[\begin{aligned}-0.256 \\ 4.096\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.124 \\ 1.519\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
